notes.text:
This update for parted fixes the following issues:

- CVE-2026-89085: heap-based buffer overflow via crafted FAT32 filesystem image (bsc#1286017).
- CVE-2026-89088: denial of service via heap buffer overflow during FAT16 resize (bsc#1286018).

notes.text: A flaw was found in parted. A heap-based buffer overflow can occur when processing a specially crafted FAT32 filesystem due to an integer calculation error during buffer allocation. A local attacker could exploit this by enticing a user or automated service to open a malicious filesystem image, resulting in an application crash leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) or potential memory corruption.

notes.text: A flaw was found in parted. A heap-based buffer overflow exists in libparted's file system resizing logic when handling FAT16 volumes. By convincing a user or administrator to resize a specially crafted FAT16 file system image with malformed directory metadata, an attacker can trigger an oversized read into a fixed-size memory buffer. This issue causes memory corruption, resulting in an application crash and a denial of service (DoS).
